story.title: (ENR SUCC) DEV & TEST - 834E/U AR PASSE Transaction Effective Date Logic Update - EDI
story.description:
Overview
This feature details the functionality required to correct the improper entry of split spans in Facets, based on Eligibility Date and Assessment Date, for changes received via EDI 834 E and U.
Business Rules & Requirements
The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date 2000 Loop (DTP*356/DTP*348) from the EDI 834 as the transaction effective date for all new enrollments, regardless of the Assessment Date. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date = 1/24/25, use Eligibility Date (1/31/25).
The business needs to utilize the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility, if the Assessment Date has changed. For example: Eligibility Date = 1/31/25 and Assessment Date changes to 6/29/25, use Assessment Date (6/29/25).
The business needs to update the Assessment Date as the transaction effective date for changes to current eligibility when the Assessment Date changes, but none of the other elements listed below have changed:Assessment Number
Assessment Tier
Assessment Division
Aid Category
Rate Cell
Pregnancy
The business needs to utilize the Eligibility Date as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received prior to the Eligibility Date.
The business needs to utilize the Maintenance Date (DTP*303) as the transaction effective date for any changes to the items listed in Requirement 3 above, when the Assessment Date does NOT change, and those changes are received after the Eligibility Date.
Current State
Currently, Maintenance effective date is being used to split spans on Update files. This is causing mismatches with capitation calculations, and the Finance team is misreporting revenue.
What is Changing
The Maintenance Date 2000 Loop (DTP*303) cannot be used for all change transactions. Depending on the change, and whether it is received prior to or after the initial Eligibility Date, the transaction effective date may reflect either the Assessment Date, Eligibility Date, or Maintenance Date.
Future State
The Maintenance Date will no longer be used to split spans based on Update (834) files, except as detailed in Requirement 4 above. The transaction dates in Facets will conform to the functionality detailed in Requirements 1-5.
Assumptions
None identified.
Dependencies/Considerations
None identified.
Risks
None identified.
Examples / Scenarios
ScenarioEligibility Started?Transaction Effective DateNew enrollment (Future eligibility date) No Eligibility Date Current eligibility, Assessment Date changed Yes Assessment Date Assessment Date changed, No changes to relevant fields Yes Assessment Date Future eligibility date, Changes to relevant fields, Assessment Date unchanged No Eligibility Date Current eligibility, Changes to relevant fields, Assessment Date unchanged Yes Maintenance Date Relevant fields include Assessment Number, Assessment Tier, Assessment Division, Aid Category, Rate Cell, Pregnancy.
Technical Notes
Data values are contained in the 834 transaction loops as follows:Assessment Date - Loop 2300, HD03
Effective Date - Loop 2000, DTP03
Maintenance Date - Loop 2000, DTP01
Adjust logic to selectively use Eligibility Date, Assessment Date, or Maintenance Date as transaction effective date based on the outlined business rules.
Ensure backward compatibility with existing EDI processing where applicable.
When multiple dates come in, use the first one.
Refer to DMND0031922.
story.acceptancecriteria:
Acceptance Criteria
EDI is able to identify the following dates in the EDI 834 file (existing functionality): Effective Date, Assessment Date, Maintenance Date.
Enrollment IT can populate any of the three dates above into the transaction effective date in Facets (existing functionality).
Given an inbound EDI 834 file, if the member’s eligibility span has not yet begun, the Eligibility Date (DTP*356/DTP*348) populates as the transaction effective date.
Given an inbound EDI 834 file, if the member’s eligibility span has already begun and the Assessment Date has changed, the Assessment Date populates as the transaction effective date.
Given an inbound EDI 834 file, if the Assessment Date has changed and none of the relevant fields have changed, the Assessment Date populates as the transaction effective date, maintaining values of relevant fields.
Given an inbound EDI 834 file, if the member’s eligibility span has not yet begun and any relevant fields have changed but Assessment Date has NOT changed, the Eligibility Date populates as the transaction effective date.
Given an inbound EDI 834 file, if the member’s eligibility span has already begun and any relevant fields have changed but Assessment Date has NOT changed, the Maintenance Date (DTP*303) populates as the transaction effective date.
QA Regression Testing
Test inbound 834 files with varying combinations of Eligibility Date, Assessment Date changes, and relevant field changes to verify correct transaction effective date population.
Verify no change in capitation calculations and accurate reporting for finance team.
Confirm that Maintenance Date is only used when specified in acceptance criteria.
Definition of Done (DoD)
All functionality detailed in the feature has been developed, implemented, and tested in Production.
Transaction effective date in Facets is correctly populated per the detailed business rules and requirements.
Code is reviewed and meets coding standards.
Unit and integration tests have passed.
User acceptance testing has been completed and approved.
Relevant documentation has been updated.

review.feedback: The set covers the core rule paths and includes negative/edge scenarios, but it needs consolidation and one grounding fix. Collapse TS_007 into existing rule scenarios because its three U-file conditions are just a regression restatement of TS_002/TS_003/TS_004, and collapse TS_008 into the scenarios that already exercise each winning-date rule because it repeats the same three rule outcomes only to assert downstream finance impact. Also fix TS_009 so it is actually grounded in the story/domain hints by naming the staging and archive paths it claims to verify, instead of saying 'named staging and archive locations' without the locations. Keep TS_003 and TS_004 as parameterized relevant-field scenarios; that shape is correct.
gaps: Under-collapsed redundancy: TS_007 duplicates existing rule coverage from TS_002, TS_003, and TS_004 and should be collapsed rather than kept as a separate backward-compatibility scenario.

Under-collapsed redundancy: TS_008 replays the same three winning-date rule paths already covered elsewhere only to assert finance impact; collapse this validation into the rule scenarios that select Eligibility Date, Assessment Date, and Maintenance Date.

Grounding gap: TS_009 says it verifies processing through the 'named staging and archive locations' but the description does not include the actual locations provided in domain hints (\\daycrtappfs01\EdifecsSTRoot\834\Inbound and \\daycrtappfs01\EdifecsSTArchive\834\Inbound\AR), so the scenario is not fully grounded to the named downstream locations it claims to test.
strengths: Core acceptance criteria are covered by TS_001-TS_006, including all three selectable date sources and the main Eligibility/Assessment/Maintenance decision rules.
TS_003 and TS_004 correctly use one parameterized scenario each for the relevant fields, named groupings, and all-fields case rather than splitting them into many near-duplicates.
The set includes both Negative and Edge coverage, especially the explicit guard that Maintenance Date must not be used outside its allowed rule path in TS_005.
